input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: GRIMBERGEN. Summary: Concession Collection of Textiles Via Textile Containers at Locations in the Municipality of Grimbergen. Description: The concessionaire is responsible for the collection via textile containers and the processing of household textile waste in the municipality of Grimbergen. The collection takes place via textile containers at various locations in the public domain and, if necessary, private land that is publicly accessible. Door-to-door collection is not part of this concession order. The concession holder pays a concession fee per ton of textile waste and receives in return for the services provided collection and processing of these textiles, the right to dispose of the collected textiles. The concessionaire is responsible for the collection and processing of the textiles at his own expense, including the non-reused and/or non-recycled portion. The The concession holder must also be responsible for clearing up illegal dumping next to these textile containers. The annual volume of textile waste can be estimated based on the number of inhabitants of the municipality of Grimbergen (40,000 inhabitants). According to the statistics from OVAM, approximately 10 kg of textile waste is selectively collected per citizen per year. In 2024, 384 tons of textiles were collected in the municipality of Grimbergen, which is in line with the OVAM averages. The concessionaire is responsible for: inform about the expected collection potential. Category (CPV code): Refuse recycling services (90514000). Published Date: 2025-11-06. Closing Date: 2025-11-25. Description of the services to be executed: this market follows the creation of twelve karst monographs, of which eleven published, Regarding the Basins of the upstream Meuse, the Lesse, the Hoyoux and the Soliere, the Haute-Meuse and the Ourthe. Karst monographs by limestone sub-basins constitute an essential tool to integrate and take into account the specificity of the subsoil of limestone areas in management and environmental protection, groundwater and regional planning. They are also part of the priority actions of the Vesdre river contract by contributing in particular to a better consideration by all the actors of the problem of the problematic groundwater in the management of the basin, water resources (catchments), but also flood problems. Summary: Modelling, Projecting and Tracking Emissions Reduction Pathways in Light of the Second Global Stocktake by 2028. Description: The IPCC 6th Assessment Report emphasizes the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions this decade to keep global warming within 1.5 degrees above pre-industrial levels. This was highlighted by the first Global Stocktake (GST) in 2023, which emphasised that limiting global warming to 1.5°C with no or limited overshoot requires deep, rapid and sustained reductions in emissions of 43% reduction in emissions by 2030 and 60% by 2035 compared to 2019 levels, aiming for net zero CO2 emissions by 2050 and that mitigation efforts embedded within the wider development context can increase the pace, depth and breadth of emissions reductions. As we reach the midpoint of this critical decade for climate action, substantial efforts are required to meet the Paris Agreement goals. The period for this project will see the submission of new Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) for 2035 by parties to the Paris agreement, the IPCC-s 7th Assessment report, and the second Global Stocktake in 2028. The second GST will also assess how national action is closing the ambition and implementation gap towards limiting warming to 1.5 degrees. This project aims to enhance the capacity of emerging economies to model GHG emissions and pathways, to improve tracking of progress towards domestic and global targets and to support the analysis and development of domestic targets, policies and measures to cut net emissions.
